method: Every regular file in the extracted archive was read, hashed as a git blob object (sha1 over "blob <len>\0" + content) and compared against the sha the recursive git tree records for the same path. The comparison runs in both directions, so a file present in one and absent from the other is caught as well as a byte difference.

archiveEntryNameSafety.note: Entry names were listed and screened before anything was written to disk, so a traversal or absolute-path entry would have aborted the ingest rather than escaping the extraction directory.

resultStatement: All 967 blobs reconcile byte-for-byte. The archive contains no file the tree does not record, the tree records no file the archive lacks, and no file differs in content.
normalizedManifestDefinition: sha256 over the newline-joined, path-sorted list of "<git blob sha>  <path>" lines covering every regular file. Independent of extraction order, timestamps and file modes.

doubleFetch.note: The archive was fetched twice in independent requests and the two responses compared byte-for-byte, not merely by digest.

nonclaims: Reconciliation establishes that the archive faithfully represents the git tree at the pinned commit. It establishes nothing about the contents being safe, buildable, or fit for any purpose.
